Hi Sanjay / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the time on today's call. Wanted to capture our discussion while it's fresh and confirm next steps so we keep momentum on the POC and reserved capacity conversation. Below is a concise recap and an initial onboarding roadmap.

Summary of pain & goals
- Production pain: inference latency spikes and unpredictable tail latency at peak batch loads (affects real-time triage workflows).
- Isolation need: MedGenix requires tenant isolation and VPC-level controls for PHI-adjacent workloads.
- Goal: Move to a reserved GPU pool that provides predictable throughput for the primary model rollout, with a plan for safe burst capacity and clear SLA targets.

Committed targets we discussed
- Baseline throughput: 8-12 concurrent streams for 8k context model (approx 4x current usage).
- SLO: 99th pct token latency target <= 220ms for single-token streaming requests; 95th pct <= 120ms.
- Uptime expectation: enterprise SLA target of 99.95% for dedicated pool.

Technical constraints called out
- Data residency: primary region US-west (we discussed VPC private control plane + customer-managed NAT).
- KV-caching: prefer persistent prefix caching for clinical templates (replay reduction).
- Model variants: need fallback plan to a smaller quantized variant for low-cost bursts.

Immediate next actions (owner / ETA)
1) Redwood to share a short scope doc + procurement checklist (attachment) — owner: Laura — ETA: 2026-09-06 EOD.
2) Redwood SE deep-dive: latency profile & preliminary GPU sizing (Aditya) — ETA: 2026-09-09.
3) MedGenix to send current qps/peak traces and any SOC2 evidence needs (Sanjay) — ETA: 2026-09-08.
4) Align on contract window and committed capacity numbers for internal approvals (Marissa + Laura) — target: 2026-09-14.

Attachments: MedGenix_MA_POC_scope.pdf (scope + runbook), redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx

I added Aditya and Marissa to help with sizing and procurement because they'll be on the follow-ups. If any of the technical points above need correction, flag now and we'll update.

Would 30 minutes on Tuesday (2026-09-08) at 10am PT work for the SE deep-dive?

Hi Sanjay / Laura / Alyssa —

Thanks for confirming the cadence. A few notes from the SE perspective after reviewing the notes and a short look at the model family you mentioned:

Initial sizing guidance (ballpark)
- For steady-state: 3 x NVIDIA A40-equivalent instances with a dedicated 16GB KV-cache pool should hit the 8-12 concurrent streams for the 8k context model with room for headroom.
- Burst plan: allow 2x burst capacity via autoscale-to-burst (adds additional pre-warmed nodes, billing only when warmed).

SLA implications
- 99.95% uptime is achievable with dedicated pool + multi-az placement; however, multi-az adds networking and cross-AZ egress considerations. We'll outline tradeoffs in the POA.

Security/data residency
- KV cache can be configured to persist to customer-managed EBS in the VPC or stored encrypted with customer KMS — both supported.

Deliverables for the Tuesday SE deep-dive
- A 2-slide latency profile snapshot + expected tail behavior on A40/A100-equivalents.
- A preliminary cost range for 6-month reserved commitment (showing reserved vs on-demand delta).
- Config options for isolation (VPC + private control plane steps).

I'm attaching a very short sketch of the sizing logic (embedded in the POC scope PDF you have). I'll expand during the call.
